title: Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat on iOS: choose style and format, and apply a brand kit, for visual creations
summary: The briefing passes: the roadmap facts, licensing gate and governance controls are supported. It correctly distinguishes the planned iOS feature from the documented desktop and web experience; the statement about existing image generation needs one additional citation.

claims.claim: This item concerns Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat visual creations.
claims.quote: Microsoft Copilot (Microsoft 365): [Copilot Chat] Apply your brand kit and style to visual creations

claims.claim: Microsoft plans built-in choices for the preferred visual style.
claims.quote: Easily customize your prompt output with built-in controls to select your preferred style

claims.claim: The planned format choices include posters, infographics and images.
claims.quote: choose the format, whether it’s a poster, infographic, or image.

claims.claim: Brand kits can contain approved logos, colour palettes, fonts, images and templates.
claims.quote: Brand kits can include logos, color palettes, fonts, images, and templates. Users can use these assets to create branded content or add approved brand assets to existing designs, presentations, and images.

claims.claim: The release notes describe this feature as available for Windows, Mac and web.
claims.quote: Apply brand kit and style to visual creations in Copilot chat [Windows, Mac, Web]

claims.claim: The documented desktop and web experience reaches style choices through the image generation capability in the + menu.
claims.quote: Add the image generation capability from the + menu so you can choose a preferred visual style.

claims.where: What's changing; licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: The release notes allow licensed Microsoft 365 Copilot users to apply their organisation's brand kit.
claims.quote: Users with a Microsoft 365 Copilot license can apply their organization's brand kit directly, eliminating the need to upload assets or describe styles manually.

claims.claim: Microsoft Learn does not yet describe the iOS version of this specific feature.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot Chat iOS brand kit style format 506755; iOS brand kit default style admin enable. Opened release notes, brand kit governance, Copilot admin settings and requirements; the matching release entry names Windows, Mac and Web, not iOS.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; What's changing; Why it matters
claims.claim: Microsoft has not stated what this feature does on arrival on iOS, so its default state is unknown.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot Chat iOS brand kit default style admin enable; 506755 default rollout. Read roadmap description, release notes, brand kit governance and Copilot admin settings; none states this iOS feature's arrival default.

claims.claim: The desktop and web release notes entry documents no admin step to switch this feature on.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot Chat iOS brand kit default style admin enable. Opened the complete matching July 1 release entry and Copilot admin settings; the release entry gives user steps, not an administrator enablement step.

claims.claim: No source found says existing behaviour changes for users who do not open the new choices.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot Chat iOS brand kit default style admin enable; 506755 default rollout. Read roadmap description, matching release entry and Copilot settings; none describes changes for users who do not choose the new controls.

claims.claim: Configured brand managers receive a publish button to share official kits with the organisation.
claims.quote: After the policy is configured, brand managers see a publish button in their brand kits that they can use to share brand kits with the organization.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: Published official kits are usable by eligible users outside the two policy groups.
claims.quote: A | No | No | Can use published official brand kits but can't create or edit brand kits.

claims.claim: Brand kit governance is configured using Cloud Policy in the Microsoft 365 Apps admin center rather than directly on the Copilot settings page.
claims.quote: Built-in Create features aren't configured individually. To make organization brand kits available in Create, set up the applicable Cloud Policy. See Configure brand kit governance and organizational assets.

claims.claim: Official brand kit governance is at Microsoft 365 Apps admin center > Customization > Policy Management > policy > Policies > Elevated role for Brand Managers.
claims.quote: select Customization > Policy Management. ... Select an existing tenant-level policy ... Select the Policies tab. ... select Elevated role for Brand Managers.

claims.claim: Automation for the Elevated role for Brand Managers policy is not yet documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Elevated role for Brand Managers Graph API PowerShell Cloud Policy automation; Microsoft Graph Cloud Policy brand manager brand kit creation API settings PowerShell. Read governance, copilotPolicySetting supported settings and TCM Copilot resources; no matching operation.

claims.claim: The Brand Manager policy is enabled with the mail-enabled security group's email address to give members policy access.
claims.quote: Set the policy to Enabled. ... In Security group email address, enter the email address of the brand manager security group.

claims.claim: The Brand Manager policy defaults to Not configured.
claims.quote: By default, the policy is set to Not configured.

claims.claim: Brand kit policy changes can take up to 24 hours to take effect.
claims.quote: Policy changes can take up to 24 hours to take effect.

claims.claim: Personal kit creation is configured at Microsoft 365 Apps admin center > Customization > Policy Management > policy > Start with the basics > Choose the scope > Configure Settings > Restrict brand kit creation.
claims.quote: select Customization > Policy Management. ... Select an existing tenant-level policy ... Start with the basics ... Choose the scope ... Configure Settings ... Select Restrict brand kit creation.

claims.claim: Automation for Restrict brand kit creation is not yet documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Restrict brand kit creation Graph API PowerShell Cloud Policy automation; Microsoft Graph Cloud Policy brand manager brand kit creation API settings PowerShell. Read governance, copilotPolicySetting supported settings and TCM Copilot resources; no matching operation.

claims.where: controls[1].note; controls[1].scope; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: The tenant-level creation policy is configured with Configuration setting Enabled and the permitted security group's email address.
claims.quote: Select an existing tenant-level policy ... set Configuration setting to Enabled. ... enter the email address of the security group whose members can create brand kits in Security group email address.

claims.claim: Users outside the permitted creation group do not see the option to create a brand kit.
claims.quote: Users outside this group don't see the option to create a brand kit.

claims.claim: The policy table says a user in neither group can use published official kits but cannot create or edit kits.
claims.quote: A | No | No | Can use published official brand kits but can't create or edit brand kits.

claims.claim: Group ownership alone does not grant permission to publish or edit official kits.
claims.quote: Group membership grants policy access. Group owners can manage the group, but ownership alone doesn't grant permission to publish or edit official brand kits.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance controls
claims.claim: The two brand kit policies are independent.
claims.quote: Microsoft Copilot provides two independent policies for brand kit governance

claims.claim: A brand manager outside the creation group cannot create or edit kits under the documented policy configuration.
claims.quote: C | No | Yes | Can't create or edit brand kits because the creation policy requirement isn't satisfied.

claims.claim: Publishing a personal kit as official requires satisfying both policy checks.
claims.quote: To publish a personal brand kit as an official brand kit, a user must satisfy both policy checks.

claims.claim: A user outside the permitted group who receives a shared kit with edit rights can only view it.
claims.quote: If a user who isn't in the permitted group receives a shared brand kit with edit rights, the user can only view the kit.

claims.claim: The restricted user sees a message saying the admin restricted brand kit creation and editing.
claims.quote: Your admin has restricted the rights for brand kit creation and editing. Please contact your admin for permission.
